newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks down, bearish trend to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks down, bearish trend to continue.

text.p: Croatian stocks took a further dip in light trade on Thursday, and analysts said they could see no end to the bearish period, as the big buyers were staying away from the market.
"Foreign investors were scared away by latest political developments, so they backed out," said Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage.
Croatia has been shaken by a wave of strikes, and last week its capital saw the biggest popular protest in years.
Kos predicted further losses for all stocks except for the fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka. Drugs firm Pliva will fluctuate around its current price, he said.
All seven traded issues fell. Volume was more than doubled at 4,938 units, turnover sligtly higher at 1.6 million kuna.
Biggest decliner, Zagrebacka Banka E-series preference stock, plunged 70 kuna to 360 with 60 shares sold.
Zagrebacka Banka lost 10 kuna to 990 on volume of 514 units. Another fully listed issue, Pliva, fell 199 kuna to 12,801, selling only two shares.
Most actively traded, food processor Podravka, closed at 195 kuna, down five, on volume of 3,995 units.
Confectioner Kras edged down 30 kuna to 420, with 255 units sold. Traders said the stock reached the perceived bottom, and could post further losses only on smaller volumes.
Hotelier Jadranturist inched down five kuna to 265, trading 25 shares. Another hotel stock Laguna Porec, down 20 kuna to 1,030, sold 147 shares.
